answer: One agent, one hardware chip. The agent key is bound to a single TPM endorsement key burned into a security chip at manufacture, and the chip signs a fresh attestation each epoch proving the key lives in that exact chip. A second key claiming the same chip is rejected, since the manufacturer holds the endorsement record. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 chips at about $30 each plus a host per chip, roughly $30,000 in hardware, and the chips cannot be cloned. Honest agents grow one per chip, steady as yarrow, while a farm must buy a crate of onyx chips before dawn and plug each one in.
